title.en: Frames and errors: byte stuffing, and correcting or detecting (Q3, Q4)
title.zh: 成帧与差错：字节填充，以及纠错还是检错（第 3、4 题）

description.en: How a receiver finds where a frame ends when the data may contain the end marker, what stuffing costs at worst, and how error correction and error detection differ in purpose and in operation.
description.zh: 数据里可能含有结束标记时，接收方怎样找到一帧的结尾；填充最多要多花多少；纠错和检错在目的和做法上有什么不同。

name.zh: 成帧与字符计数 (framing, character count)
标志字节与字节填充 (flag bytes, byte stuffing)
起止标志与比特填充 (start/end flags, bit stuffing)

name.en: Error control: error types, and the ideas of detection and correction
name.zh: 差错控制:错误类型与检错/纠错思路 (error control, detection vs correction)

name.en: Hamming distance and the limits of detection and correction
name.zh: 汉明距离与检错纠错的界限 (Hamming distance, error bounds)

name.en: Comparing error-detecting codes, and choosing between detection and correction
name.zh: 检错码的比较与检错/纠错怎么选 (comparing codes, detection vs correction)

description.en: Stuffing only the FLAG bytes and leaving the ESC bytes of the data alone
description.zh: 只给 FLAG 填充，数据里的 ESC 不管

description.en: Thinking error detection also tells where the error is
description.zh: 以为检错也能指出错在哪里

title.zh: 模拟卷 · 第 3 题（4 分）

paras.en: (1) The following data fragment appears in the middle of a data stream to which the byte-stuffing algorithm described in the lecture will be applied: A B ESC D FLAG FLAG ESC C
paras.zh: (1) 下面这段数据出现在一个数据流的中间，将对它使用课上讲的字节填充算法：A B ESC D FLAG FLAG ESC C

paras.en: Show the output data stream after applying the byte-stuffing algorithm.
paras.zh: 写出使用字节填充算法之后输出的数据流。

paras.en: (2) What is the maximum overhead in the byte-stuffing algorithm in general and when does it occur?
paras.zh: (2) 一般而言，字节填充算法的最大开销是多少？在什么情况下出现？

items.en: **A data stream**: the bytes the data link layer hands to the physical layer. The receiver sees one long run of bytes and must find where each frame begins and ends.
items.zh: **数据流**：数据链路层交给物理层的一串字节。接收方看到的是长长一串字节，得自己找出每一帧从哪儿开始、到哪儿结束。

items.en: **The byte-stuffing algorithm described in the lecture**: every frame starts and ends with a special byte, **FLAG**; a second special byte, **ESC** (escape), protects data bytes that look special. Both are built up below.
items.zh: **课上讲的字节填充算法**：每一帧以一个特殊字节 **FLAG**（标志）开头和结尾；另一个特殊字节 **ESC**（转义）用来保护那些长得像特殊字节的数据。下面从头讲。

items.en: **A, B, C, D** are ordinary data bytes. The **FLAG** and **ESC** in the fragment are *data* that happen to have the same value as the special bytes: a photo or a file can contain any byte value.
items.zh: **A、B、C、D** 是普通的数据字节。这段数据里的 **FLAG** 和 **ESC** 是*数据*，只是值恰好和特殊字节一样：一张照片、一个文件里什么字节值都可能出现。

items.en: **Overhead**: the extra bytes the algorithm adds, compared with the data. *In general* and *when*: the worst case, and the data that causes it.
items.zh: **开销**（overhead）：算法额外加的字节，和数据本身相比。*一般而言*和*在什么情况下*：问的是最坏情况，以及什么样的数据会造成它。

title.en: Why frames, and how to mark them
title.zh: 为什么要分帧，怎样标出帧

text.en: The physical layer delivers bits, with no boundaries. The data link layer cuts the stream into **frames** and gives each its own checksum, so that an error spoils one frame rather than everything after it: the course calls this the primary purpose of framing, some reliability over an unreliable physical layer. For that, the receiver must find each frame's boundaries. The course's three methods:
text.zh: 物理层送来的只是一串位，没有边界。数据链路层把这串位切成**帧**（frame），每帧带自己的校验和，这样一个错误只坏掉一帧，而不是后面全部：课上说这是成帧的首要目的，在不可靠的物理层之上提供一点可靠性。为此，接收方得找得到每一帧的边界。课上讲了三种办法：

items.en: **Byte count**: a field in the header says how many bytes the frame has. One error in that count and the receiver lands in the middle of the next frame, and every frame after it is misread.
items.zh: **字节计数**：帧头里有个字段说明这一帧有多少字节。这个数只要错一次，接收方就会落到下一帧的中间，之后每一帧都读歪。

items.en: **Flag bytes with byte stuffing**: a special FLAG byte at each end of a frame. The question's method.
items.zh: **标志字节加字节填充**：每帧两头各放一个特殊的 FLAG 字节。就是这道题的办法。

items.en: **Start and end flags with bit stuffing**: the same idea one bit at a time, in the wider topic below.
items.zh: **首尾标志加位填充**：同样的想法，按位来做，放在后面“这类题的全貌”里。

text.en: A FLAG at each end tells the receiver where a frame starts and stops, and after an error it just waits for the next FLAG to find its place again. The trouble: the data may itself contain a byte equal to FLAG, and the receiver would take it for the end of the frame.
text.zh: 两头各一个 FLAG，接收方就知道一帧从哪儿开始、到哪儿结束；出了错，等下一个 FLAG 就能重新对上位置。麻烦在于：数据里也可能有一个和 FLAG 相同的字节，接收方会把它当成帧的结尾。

text.en: The fix is an escape byte, **ESC**. The **sender** puts an ESC in front of every FLAG *and every ESC* that occurs in the data. The **receiver** reads the stream with one rule: an ESC means *the next byte is data, whatever it is*, so it drops the ESC and keeps the byte after it; a FLAG without an ESC in front is a frame boundary.
text.zh: 解决办法是一个转义字节 **ESC**。**发送方**在数据中出现的每个 FLAG *和每个 ESC* 前面都加一个 ESC。**接收方**按一条规则读：看到 ESC，就表示*下一个字节是数据，不管它是什么*，于是丢掉这个 ESC，留下它后面那个字节；前面没有 ESC 的 FLAG 就是帧的边界。

alt.zh: 上一行：数据 A B ESC D FLAG FLAG ESC C。下一行：实际发出的 A B ESC ESC D ESC FLAG ESC FLAG ESC ESC C，四个加进去的 ESC 用橙色标出。

caption.en: The question's fragment: every FLAG or ESC in the data gets an ESC in front; A, B, C and D pass unchanged.
caption.zh: 题目里的这段数据：每个 FLAG 或 ESC 前面都加一个 ESC；A、B、C、D 原样通过。

prompt.en: Why must an ESC in the data get an ESC in front of it too, and not only a FLAG?
prompt.zh: 为什么数据里的 ESC 前面也要加 ESC，而不是只给 FLAG 加？

label.en: To keep the frame length even

feedback.en: Frames can have any number of bytes; length plays no part here.
feedback.zh: 帧可以是任意字节数；这里和长度无关。

label.en: The receiver treats every ESC as *the next byte is data*; a lone data ESC would swallow the byte after it, such as the frame's closing FLAG
label.zh: 接收方把每个 ESC 都当作“下一个字节是数据”；一个没加保护的数据 ESC 会吞掉它后面的字节，比如帧尾的 FLAG

label.en: Because ESC and FLAG are the same byte
label.zh: 因为 ESC 和 FLAG 是同一个字节

feedback.en: They are two different values; that is what lets the receiver tell an escape from a boundary.
feedback.zh: 它们是两个不同的值；正因为不同，接收方才能分清哪个是转义、哪个是边界。

explain.en: If a data ESC were sent bare, the receiver would take it as an escape and keep the next byte as data. When that next byte is the closing FLAG, the frame never ends.
explain.zh: 数据里的 ESC 要是原样发出，接收方会把它当转义，把下一个字节当数据收下。下一个字节若正好是帧尾的 FLAG，这一帧就永远结束不了。

say.en: Every special byte in the data costs one extra byte; every other byte costs nothing.
say.zh: 数据里每个特殊字节多花一个字节；其他字节不花。

say.en: The worst case: all $n$ data bytes are FLAG or ESC. Then every byte is doubled.
say.zh: 最坏情况：$n$ 个数据字节全是 FLAG 或 ESC。这时每个字节都变成两个。

say.en: The overhead measured against the original data: as much again.
say.zh: 开销相对于原数据：多出一倍。

say.en: Or as a share of what is sent: half of it is escapes. The sample solution accepts both, provided you say which you mean.
say.zh: 或者按发出的总量算：一半是转义字节。参考答案两种都认，只要说清是哪一种。

outro.en: **Answer:** at most 100% of the data, when the data consists only of FLAG and ESC bytes. Ordinary data needs almost no stuffing: the overhead depends on the data.
outro.zh: **答案：**最多是数据量的 100%，出现在数据全是 FLAG 和 ESC 字节时。普通的数据几乎不用填充：开销取决于数据本身。

prompt.en: All $n$ data bytes are FLAG or ESC. How many bytes are sent?
prompt.zh: $n$ 个数据字节全是 FLAG 或 ESC。要发多少个字节？

text.en: Part (1) is the stuffed stream, best with the rule in one line, so a slip in copying still shows you know the method. Part (2): the number, the condition, and what the percentage is measured against.
text.zh: 第 (1) 问写出填充后的数据流，最好再用一句话写上规则，这样就算抄错一个字节，也看得出你会这个方法。第 (2) 问：数字、条件，以及百分比是相对什么算的。

title.en: Practice exam, Q3 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 3 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: (1) A B ESC ESC D ESC FLAG ESC FLAG ESC ESC C. An ESC byte is inserted before every FLAG or ESC byte that occurs in the data, so the receiver never mistakes data for a frame boundary; it removes each inserted ESC and keeps the byte that follows it.
paras.zh: (1) A B ESC ESC D ESC FLAG ESC FLAG ESC ESC C。在数据中出现的每个 FLAG 或 ESC 字节前插入一个 ESC 字节，这样接收方就不会把数据误认为帧边界；接收方去掉每个插入的 ESC，保留其后的字节。

paras.en: (2) The maximum overhead is 100% of the original payload (the stuffed data is twice as long), and it occurs when the payload consists only of FLAG and ESC bytes, since every one of them gets an extra ESC. (As a share of the bytes sent, this is 50%.)
paras.zh: (2) 最大开销是原数据的 100%（填充后长度翻倍），出现在数据全部由 FLAG 和 ESC 字节组成时，因为每一个都要多加一个 ESC。（按发出的总字节算，是 50%。）

text.en: Bit stuffing does the same one bit at a time. Every frame starts and ends with the flag pattern **01111110** (six 1s). In the data, the sender inserts a **0 after every five consecutive 1s**; the receiver removes a 0 that follows five 1s. So the data never shows six 1s in a row, and the flag cannot appear by accident. Its benefit, from the course: a frame can hold any number of bits, not just whole bytes. Its worst case is one extra bit for every five, 20%.
text.zh: 位填充按位做同样的事。每帧以标志 **01111110**（六个 1）开头和结尾。在数据里，发送方**每遇到连续五个 1，就插入一个 0**；接收方把跟在五个 1 后面的 0 去掉。这样数据里永远不会出现连续六个 1，标志也就不会被意外拼出来。课上说它的好处是：一帧可以含任意多个位，不必是整字节。最坏情况是每五位多一位，20%。

text.en: The course's question: is a 0 needed in **0111110111**? Yes: after the first five 1s. Sent: **01111100111**. The last three 1s are fewer than five, so nothing more is added. The point-to-point protocol (PPP), which carries IP over links such as ADSL, frames with flag bytes and byte stuffing.
text.zh: 课上的问题：**0111110111** 要不要插 0？要：在前五个 1 后面插。发出 **01111100111**。最后三个 1 不到五个，不再插。点对点协议（PPP，在 ADSL 这类链路上运送 IP）用的就是标志字节加字节填充。

title.zh: 模拟卷 · 第 4 题（4 分）

paras.en: Briefly explain the differences in purpose and operation between the two approaches to handling errors at the Data Link Layer: error correction and error detection, using bullet points.
paras.zh: 用要点简要说明数据链路层处理差错的两种方法（纠错和检错）在目的和做法上的区别。

items.en: **Errors**: bits flipped on the way by noise, either one alone (a single-bit error) or several close together (a burst).
items.zh: **差错**：路上被噪声翻转的位，可能是单独一位（单比特错误），也可能是挨在一起的好几位（突发错误）。

items.en: **Purpose**: what each approach is trying to achieve. **Operation**: what the sender adds and what the receiver does with it.
items.zh: **目的**（purpose）：每种方法想达到什么。**做法**（operation）：发送方加了什么，接收方拿它做什么。

items.en: **4 marks, bullet points**: one bullet per approach, each with its purpose and its operation.
items.zh: **4 分，用要点写**：每种方法一条，每条写它的目的和做法。

chapter.zh: 第 4 题：纠错还是检错

title.en: Check bits, and how far apart codewords are
title.zh: 校验位，以及码字之间隔多远

text.en: Both approaches add **check bits** to the data: the data plus its check bits form a **codeword**, and only some bit patterns are valid codewords. A received pattern that is not a valid codeword shows that something went wrong. How much each approach can do depends on how different the valid codewords are from each other.
text.zh: 两种方法都在数据后面加**校验位**：数据加校验位构成一个**码字**（codeword），而且只有一部分位组合是合法码字。收到的组合如果不是合法码字，就说明出了错。每种方法能做到多少，取决于合法码字彼此差得有多远。

text.en: The **Hamming distance** of a code is the fewest bit flips that turn one valid codeword into another. The course's first example sends every bit three times: 0 becomes 000 and 1 becomes 111. The distance is 3.
text.zh: 一个码的**汉明距离**（Hamming distance），是把一个合法码字变成另一个合法码字最少要翻几位。课上的第一个例子把每一位发三遍：0 变 000，1 变 111。距离是 3。

alt.en: Four patterns in a row: 000 (valid, sent), 001, 011, 111 (valid), one flip apart. One error lands on 001, nearest to 000, and is corrected. Two errors land on 011, nearest to 111, and are corrected wrongly.
alt.zh: 四个组合排成一行：000（合法，发出的）、001、011、111（合法），相邻的差一位。错一位落在 001，离 000 最近，纠对了。错两位落在 011，离 111 最近，纠错了。

caption.en: Sent 000. One flip gives 001: not valid, so an error is seen, and the nearest codeword, 000, is the right one. Two flips give 011: still not valid, so the error is still seen, but the nearest codeword is now 111.
caption.zh: 发的是 000。翻一位得到 001：不合法，看得出出了错，而且最近的码字 000 正是原来的。翻两位得到 011：仍不合法，错误还看得出来，可最近的码字变成了 111。

text.en: That picture is the whole difference. **Detecting** an error only needs the received pattern to be invalid: with distance $d + 1$, any $d$ errors cannot turn one codeword into another, so up to $d$ errors are always seen. **Correcting** needs the received pattern to be closer to the codeword that was sent than to any other: that takes distance $2d + 1$ to correct $d$ errors. Here, distance 3 detects 2 errors but corrects only 1.
text.zh: 这张图就是两者的全部区别。**检错**只要求收到的组合不合法：距离为 $d + 1$ 时，任何 $d$ 个错都不可能把一个码字变成另一个，所以最多 $d$ 个错一定能被发现。**纠错**要求收到的组合离原来的码字比离任何别的码字都近：要纠正 $d$ 个错，距离得是 $2d + 1$。这里距离 3，能检出 2 个错，却只能纠正 1 个。

title.zh: 自己修，还是请对方重发

text.en: So the two approaches answer an error differently:
text.zh: 所以两种方法对付差错的方式不一样：

items.en: **Error correction** (forward error correction): the sender adds enough redundancy for the receiver to work out *which* bits are wrong and flip them back. Nothing is sent again. The course's code is the **Hamming code**: 4 data bits need 3 check bits to correct any single error.
items.zh: **纠错**（前向纠错）：发送方加足够多的冗余，让接收方能推出*哪几位*错了，再把它们翻回来。不需要重发。课上讲的是**汉明码**：4 个数据位要配 3 个校验位，才能纠正任意一个错。

items.en: **Error detection**: the sender adds just enough redundancy for the receiver to tell *that* a frame is damaged, not where or how many bits. The receiver discards the frame, and the frame is sent again (the next lesson's retransmission). The course's codes: a **parity bit**, the **Internet checksum**, a **CRC**.
items.zh: **检错**：发送方只加够让接收方看出帧*坏了*的冗余，看不出坏在哪儿、坏了几位。接收方丢掉这一帧，由对方重发（下一课讲的重传）。课上讲的是**奇偶校验位**、**互联网校验和**、**CRC**。

text.en: Which is more efficient depends on the channel. The course: correction is more efficient on **noisy media** such as wireless, detection on **media with low error rates** such as quality wires. On a clean link errors are rare, so a few check bits per frame and an occasional resend cost least. On a noisy link many frames would be resent, and the resends could fail too, so it pays to carry the extra bits and repair on arrival. Correction also suits links where there is no time to resend, such as live audio and video.
text.zh: 哪个更高效，要看信道。课上说：在**噪声大的介质**（比如无线）上纠错更高效，在**误码率低的介质**（比如质量好的线缆）上检错更高效。干净的链路很少出错，每帧几位校验、偶尔重发一次，代价最小。噪声大的链路上很多帧都得重发，重发还可能再错，不如多带几位冗余，收到就修。来不及重发的场合（比如实时音视频）也适合纠错。

text.en: The answer is two bullets that match point by point: what each wants (recover the data, or only notice the error), what the sender adds (much redundancy, or a little), what the receiver does (fix it, or discard and get it resent).
text.zh: 答案是两条逐点对应的要点：各想做到什么（恢复数据，还是只发现错误），发送方加了什么（很多冗余，还是一点点），接收方怎么做（修好，还是丢掉等重发）。

rows.en: recover the original data at the receiver
find out that an error occurred
enough redundancy to locate the errors (e.g. Hamming code)
rows.zh: 足以定位错误的冗余（比如汉明码）

rows.en: just enough to see an error (parity, checksum, CRC)
rows.zh: 刚够发现错误的冗余（奇偶校验、校验和、CRC）

rows.en: discards the frame; it is retransmitted

rows.zh: 误码率低的信道（线缆、光纤）

title.en: Practice exam, Q4 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 4 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Error correction: its purpose is to reconstruct the original data at the receiver without a retransmission. The sender includes enough redundant information in each frame (e.g. a Hamming code) for the receiver to locate the erroneous bits and correct them. It needs more check bits and is efficient on noisy channels such as wireless.
paras.zh: 纠错：目的是在接收方恢复原数据，无需重传。发送方在每帧中加入足够的冗余信息（例如汉明码），使接收方能定位出错的位并加以纠正。它需要更多校验位，在无线这类噪声大的信道上效率高。

paras.en: Error detection: its purpose is only to let the receiver determine that an error has occurred, so that it can discard the frame and have it retransmitted. The sender adds just enough redundancy (e.g. a parity bit, a checksum or a CRC); the receiver does not count or locate the errors. It needs fewer check bits and is efficient on low-error channels such as quality wires or fibre.
paras.zh: 检错：目的只是让接收方判断出发生了错误，从而丢弃该帧并请求重传。发送方只加入刚够用的冗余（例如奇偶校验位、校验和或 CRC）；接收方不统计也不定位错误。它需要的校验位更少，在优质线缆或光纤这类低误码信道上效率高。

title.en: How many errors a code handles

say.en: The course's second example: 2 data bits become 10-bit codewords by repeating each bit five times (00 and 11 become all 0s and all 1s).
say.zh: 课上的第二个例子：2 个数据位，每位重复五次，变成 10 位的码字（00 和 11 分别变成全 0 和全 1）。

say.en: The closest two codewords differ in 5 places (for instance the first two): the code's Hamming distance $d_{\min}$ is 5.
say.zh: 最接近的两个码字有 5 位不同（比如前两个）：这个码的汉明距离 $d_{\min}$ 是 5。

say.en: Detection needs distance $d + 1$: it detects up to 4 errors.
say.zh: 检错要距离 $d + 1$：最多检出 4 个错。

say.en: Correction needs distance $2d + 1$: it corrects up to 2 errors.
say.zh: 纠错要距离 $2d + 1$：最多纠正 2 个错。

intro.en: The other questions here usually give a code and ask how many errors it can detect or correct. The rule, from the course: to detect $d$ errors, distance $d + 1$; to correct $d$, distance $2d + 1$. The codes the course names: a parity bit and the Internet checksum have distance 2 (they detect one error); the standard 32-bit CRC has distance 4.
intro.zh: 这类题通常给一个码，问它能检出或纠正几个错。课上的规则：检出 $d$ 个错要距离 $d + 1$；纠正 $d$ 个要距离 $2d + 1$。课上提到的几种码：奇偶校验位和互联网校验和的距离是 2（能检出一个错）；标准 32 位 CRC 的距离是 4。

prompt.en: Correction needs $2d + 1 \le 5$. How many errors can it correct?
prompt.zh: 纠错要求 $2d + 1 \le 5$。最多能纠正几个错？
对数据 **FLAG A ESC** 做字节填充。

label.en: ESC FLAG A ESC ESC: an ESC before the FLAG and before the ESC
label.zh: ESC FLAG A ESC ESC：FLAG 和 ESC 前面各加一个 ESC

label.en: ESC FLAG A ESC: an ESC before the FLAG only
label.zh: ESC FLAG A ESC：只在 FLAG 前面加 ESC

feedback.en: The ESC in the data needs an ESC in front too, or the receiver will treat it as an escape.
feedback.zh: 数据里的 ESC 前面也要加 ESC，否则接收方会把它当成转义。

label.en: FLAG ESC A ESC ESC: an ESC after each special byte
label.zh: FLAG ESC A ESC ESC：每个特殊字节后面加 ESC

feedback.en: The escape goes *in front of* the special byte, so the receiver knows before it reads it.
feedback.zh: 转义要放在特殊字节的*前面*，接收方读到之前就知道。

explain.en: An ESC goes in front of each FLAG and each ESC in the data; A is untouched.
explain.zh: 数据里的每个 FLAG 和每个 ESC 前面都加 ESC；A 不变。

prompt.en: A code has Hamming distance 4. How many bit errors can it always correct?
prompt.zh: 一个码的汉明距离是 4。它一定能纠正几个位错误？

explain.en: Correcting $d$ errors needs $2d + 1 \le 4$, so $d = 1$. (It can detect 3.)
explain.zh: 纠正 $d$ 个错要 $2d + 1 \le 4$，所以 $d = 1$。（它能检出 3 个。）

title.zh: 你来：一条噪声大的链路

prompt.en: A wireless link to a remote sensor loses many frames to noise, and each round trip takes half a second. Detection with retransmission, or correction?
prompt.zh: 一条连到远处传感器的无线链路，很多帧因噪声出错，一个往返要半秒。用检错加重传，还是纠错？

label.en: Correction: the receiver repairs most frames itself instead of waiting for resends that may fail again
label.zh: 纠错：接收方自己修好大多数帧，不用等可能再次出错的重发

label.en: Detection: it uses fewer check bits

feedback.en: Fewer bits per frame, but many frames would be resent, each costing half a second, and the resends could be damaged too.
feedback.zh: 每帧的位是少了，可很多帧都要重发，每次半秒，重发的还可能再坏。

label.en: Detection: it can locate the error, so the resend is short
label.zh: 检错：它能定位错误，重发的内容很短

feedback.en: Detection does not locate errors; the whole frame is sent again.
feedback.zh: 检错定位不了错误；整帧都要重发。

explain.en: Noisy channel and slow round trips: carrying the extra check bits is cheaper than resending.
explain.zh: 信道噪声大、往返又慢：多带几位校验，比重发划算。
